messages:
sam (infra-security): Quick heads-up — we're running a tabletop sim next week to validate isolation guarantees for a segmented private deployment. Scope: VPC + on-prem variants, RBAC change that widens a role for a short window, audit log routing under air-gapped constraints, and a vuln discovered in our runtime image. Looking for quick review of the plan and any gotchas.

zoe (sec-ops): +1 to review. main things I want covered:
- deny-by-default network policies (ingress + egress)
- explicit egress only to internal collectors/proxy
- RBAC canary + immediate rollback path
- KMS/HSM key policy for audit log encryption and rotation
- proof that lateral movement is constrained (no hostNetwork exceptions unless approved) :eyes:

alan (platform): For the netpol baseline I usually start with this minimal YAML and then open specific ports per namespace. Example we use in staging:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-by-default
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  ingress: []
  egress: []
```
apply with `kubectl apply -f netpol.yaml` then add targeted allow rules.

sam (infra-security): Looks good. For on-prem with no internet egress, how are we planning to get audit logs to the SIEM?

maria (privacy): We need retention and redaction rules up front. If audit logs contain request bodies or tokens, we must either redact before forwarding or keep them in the customer-managed KMS-encrypted store with access controls. Also confirm retention period in the sim (30/90/365).

leo (crypto): For encryption, recommend envelope encryption: logs encrypted by a local key, that key is itself encrypted by the KMS/HSM key. For on-prem airgapped deployments, use an HSM or a customer-managed KMS endpoint. Minimal key policy snippet (conceptual):
```
{
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect": "Allow", "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/log-shipper"}, "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt"], "Resource": "*"}
  ]
}
```
Note: lock down `kms:ReEncrypt` and `kms:GenerateDataKey` narrowly.

devops-oncall: On rollback/fast-fail for RBAC canary: plan should include a single-step automation that reverts the role binding. e.g. `kubectl patch rolebinding /my-binding --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/subjects","value":[]}]'` as an escape hatch, and a documented runbook entry `RBAC-CANARY-ROLLBACK` in the incident repo. Test that in staging first. :thumbsup:

zoe (sec-ops): Also ensure audit logging is immutable for the sim — we flip on append-only mode in the collector and snapshot the bucket. For on-prem, we use syslog TLS to the collector: `rsyslog -> collector:6514` over mTLS. Example config line: `*.* @@10.2.3.4:6514;RSYSLOG_SyslogProtocol23Format`

sec-bot: Automated scan result: runtime image `redwood/runtime:1.14.2` flagged CVE-2024-XY12 (privilege escalation). Severity: medium. Suggested action: rebuild with patched base and run E2E. See scan ID `scan-94721`.

sam (infra-security): Good catch. We'll include vuln triage in the sim: assign severity, plan immediate mitigation (apply PSP/OPA gate, restrict capabilities), and schedule rebuild. Any quick mitigation controls we can toggle during sim?

alan (platform): We can toggle an admission controller policy to deny containers with `cap_add: SYS_ADMIN` and limit `runAsUser: 0`. That buys time. Also can use runtime seccomp profile to block known syscalls.

maria (privacy): One thing we must simulate: a data subject access request that touches audit logs. Make sure we can produce an export from the encrypted store without leaking keys (use KMS-access audit trail).

leo (crypto): For rotation during the sim, do a key rotation exercise: generate a new data key, re-wrap a small sample (not full backfill) to validate tooling. Don't rotate master KMS without a tested fallback.

devops-oncall: Incident play to include: detection (SIEM alert), containment (isolate namespace + revoke rolebinding), eradication (rebuild images + redeploy), recovery (restore traffic via canary), and postmortem with labeled action items. Keep timeboxes: containment within 15m, revoke binding within 5m of containment decision.

zoe (sec-ops): Practical gotcha: some network plugins ignore namespace-scoped netpols if `hostNetwork: true` or `hostPort` used. Ensure the sim's test apps don't use those unless intentionally testing edge-case.

sam (infra-security): Action items from here:
- zoe: finalize netpol + syslog wiring and send YAMLs (due in 48h)
- alan: prepare admission controller toggles and rollback automation (48h)
- leo: key policy and sample rotation tooling (48h)
- maria: retention/redaction checklist and DSAR runbook snippet (48h)
- devops-oncall: embed RBAC-CANARY-ROLLBACK into incident runbook and verify in staging (by sim date)
- sec-bot please re-run image scan after rebuild and post results.

sec-bot: Acknowledged. Will re-run `scan-94721` on `redwood/runtime:1.14.3` once available and post summary.

zoe (sec-ops): Sounds good. I'll create the sim doc and invite infra, platform, and privacy to the tabletop. Expect calendar invite by EOD. :calendar:

sam (infra-security): Thanks team — this looks actionable. We'll iterate on the YAMLs and run the sim with a short live attack-surface exercise (attacker emulation: lateral `kubectl exec` attempt + log exfiltration simulation). Keep logs of timeline for the postmortem.

alan (platform): Quick note: if anyone needs to run the netpol/rollback commands in staging, ping me and I'll enable dev cluster access for the day.

maria (privacy): One last privacy note — mark any simulated PII with a `SIM_` prefix, do not use real tokens in the sim.

sam (infra-security): Copy that. Closing thread for now, will post the sim doc link once created. Thanks all. :lock:
